tagline: Global producer of primary aluminum with integrated alumina operations
hero_kpi_rationale: The new smelter project in Oklahoma, in partnership with EGA, will produce 750,000 tonnes of aluminum per year, more than doubling U.S. production capacity and representing the first major new project since 1980.

kpis.name: Inola New Smelter Project
kpis.explanation: Joint development agreement with EGA to construct the first new primary aluminum smelter in the United States since 1980, located in Inola, Oklahoma.
kpis.description: The new smelter in Inola, Oklahoma, being developed with EGA (Century holds 40%, EGA holds 60%), will produce 750,000 tonnes of primary aluminum annually, more than doubling current U.S. production capacity. Construction expected to begin by end of 2026, subject to completion of detailed engineering and power agreements.
kpis.signal: Major production capacity expansion, first new US smelter in 45 years.

kpis.name: Average LME Aluminum Price
kpis.explanation: Average London Metal Exchange price for primary aluminum, a key determinant of revenue.
kpis.description: The average LME aluminum price for 2025 was $2,630 per tonne, up from $2,419 in 2024. Global macroeconomic trends and low inventory levels near all-time lows have created a supportive pricing environment.
kpis.signal: Favorable pricing environment supported by low global inventory levels and improving demand.

kpis.name: Average Midwest Premium
kpis.explanation: Regional premium for aluminum sold in the United States, reflecting tariff impact and supply dynamics.
kpis.description: The average Midwest Premium for 2025 was $1,295 per tonne, up significantly from $427 in 2024. This substantial increase resulted from the tariff increases implemented in February and May 2025, which increased tariff rates from 10% to 25% to 50%, creating material positive impact on the company's financial position.
kpis.signal: Significant increase driven by Section 232 aluminum tariff escalations, materially positive for financial results.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Total capital spending on fixed assets for maintenance and growth projects.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures for 2025 totaled $100.2 million, including maintenance and development projects. For 2026, the company estimates total capital spending of $170-180 million, including approximately $60-70 million for Grundartangi repairs (expected to be insurance-reimbursed), $45 million for Mt. Holly restart, and $25 million for Jamalco investments.
kpis.signal: Ongoing investment in plant sustainability and operational improvements.

kpis.name: Hawesville Facility Sale
kpis.explanation: Completed divestiture of Hawesville, Kentucky facility to finance domestic aluminum production expansion.
kpis.description: On February 2, 2026, the company completed the sale of its Hawesville, Kentucky facility to a Terawulf affiliate for $200.0 million in cash plus a 6.8% non-dilutive minority equity interest in the Terawulf data center development. Proceeds are intended to finance the restart of Mt. Holly's last potline and investments in the new Inola smelter project.
kpis.signal: Strategic asset sale generating capital for new smelter project and Mt. Holly potline restart.

kpis.name: IRA Section 45X Tax Credit
kpis.explanation: Advanced manufacturing production tax credit of 10% on eligible domestic aluminum production costs under Inflation Reduction Act.
kpis.description: Final regulations for Section 45X were issued on October 24, 2024. The company has recognized a receivable and corresponding offset to COGS and SG&A expenses for the 10% tax credit on eligible domestic production costs. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4, 2025, requires annual reductions of 25% beginning in 2031, phasing out to zero by 2034.
kpis.signal: Government incentive reducing production costs for domestically produced aluminum through 2033 (reduced 25% annually beginning 2031).

kpis.name: Jamalco Acquisition Gain
kpis.explanation: Non-recurring gain from acquisition of 55% interest in Jamalco joint venture with Jamaica government.
kpis.description: On May 2, 2023, the company acquired a 55% interest in Jamalco (Jamaica alumina refinery) through acquisition of General Alumina Holdings Limited. A bargain purchase gain of $245.9 million was recognized in 2024. Jamalco has approximately 1.4 million tonnes of alumina production capacity, with the company acting as managing partner and consuming the commensurate alumina off-take.
kpis.signal: Strategic acquisition providing vertical integration of alumina supply with ~1.4 million tonnes annual capacity.

kpis.name: Grundartangi Production Restart
kpis.explanation: Expected resumption of production on Grundartangi potline idled due to transformer failures in September-October 2025.
kpis.description: In October 2025, Grundartangi smelter's potline was temporarily idled due to transformer failures in September-October 2025, reducing production by approximately two-thirds. The other potline remains in full production. Production resumption is estimated to begin by end of April 2026. Losses are expected to be covered under insurance policies.
kpis.signal: Resolution of major production disruption, restoring approximately two-thirds of Grundartangi capacity.

kpis.name: U.S. Department of Energy Grant
kpis.explanation: Federal funding award for construction of new aluminum smelter under Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act.
kpis.description: On January 10, 2025, the company entered into a Cooperative Agreement with the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations for up to $500 million in Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act funding to build the new aluminum smelter in Inola, Oklahoma as part of the Industrial Demonstrations Program.
kpis.signal: Significant government support for domestic aluminum production strategic initiative.

risks.title: Aluminum Price Fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: Position in MD&A, impact on revenues, explicit discussion of pricing components and volatility

risks.title: Electrical Power Cost and Supply Risk
risks.score_rationale: Position in Risk Factors and MD&A, power represents >84% of COGS, market-based pricing exposure, transmission risks

risks.title: Foreign Currency Risk
risks.score_rationale: Exposure to ISK, EUR, CNY, JMD through operations in Iceland, Netherlands, China, Jamaica

risks.title: Regulatory and Environmental Compliance Risk
risks.score_rationale: Discussion of evolving environmental regulations and tariff policy changes (Section 232 changes in 2025)

risks.title: Project Development and Execution Risk
risks.score_rationale: New smelter project subject to numerous contingencies: detailed engineering, power agreements, definitive JV agreement, construction timeline

risks.title: Equipment Failure and Production Disruption Risk
risks.score_rationale: Recent Grundartangi transformer failures caused two-thirds production reduction; Jamalco equipment failure in 2023 resulted in $30.4M margin impact

risks.title: Litigation Risk
risks.score_rationale: Multiple ongoing legal actions noted but assessed as immaterial individually and in aggregate

risks.title: Credit and Liquidity Risk
risks.score_rationale: Debt obligations and contractual commitments including long-term power contracts extending through 2036

ai_positioning.summary: Century Aluminum does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filings. The company's data center minority interest through the Hawesville sale relates to high-performance computing infrastructure but is not positioned as an AI initiative.
